paper_metadata.title: Enhanced High-Temperature Compression Property of TiAlNb2VW0.3 Refractory High-Entropy Alloy

evidence.quote: In order to further enhance the high-temperature compression property of the AlNb2TiV refractory high-entropy alloy, the AlNb 2TiVWx (x = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5) alloys have been newly designed.

the AlNb2TiVW0.1 alloy starts to show micro-segregation with the unclear white dendritic.

attributes.composition: W and Ti enriched in primary dendritic arm; Al, Nb, V enriched in inter-dendritic region

evidence.quote: the AlNb2TiVW0.3 alloy has a clear white dendritic. The white dendritic is the primary solidification part, where there should be more high-melting point elements.

the AlNb2TiVW0.5 alloy has many cavities and a poor metallurgical quality, implying a bad property of this alloy. These cavities must be casting defects, not simply corroded holes, presenting a black hole shape.

phases_and_microstructures.name: HCP
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: compressed at 400 °C with 500 MPa initial stress

evidence.quote: Under high-temperature compression stress, the AlNb2TiV alloy exhibits the phase transformation of BCC → HCP, as shown in Fig. 5d.

we believe that, at room temperature, the addition of W mainly plays a role of solid-solution strengthening, while, at a higher temperature, the mechanism changes from solid-solution strengthening to diffusion-controlled.
